newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan gives revamped BCCI unit to UAE group.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan gives revamped BCCI unit to UAE group.

text.p: Pakistan's state Privatisation Commission on Monday transferred a revamped unit of the former Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) to a United Arab Emirates (UAE) group to complete a sale held last month.

An agreement was signed under which the commission handed over 70 percent shares worth $40.54 million of Habib Credit and Exchange Bank Ltd (HCEBL) to the UAE's Nahayan bin Mubarak Al Nahayan consortium, the official APP news agency said.
The consortium had lodged the highest bid in an auction held on June 12 for 70 percent equity stake in HCEBL, which was once part of the collapsed BCCI.
Full payment was received by the State (central) Bank of Pakistan on June 26, APP said.
The group had first offered the highest bid of 38 rupees per share for 42 million shares of the total 60 million shares but, in later talks, raised the bid price to 39 rupees per share.
The government will retain 20 percent of the HCEBL's shares and 10 percent will be offered to the bank's employees.

HCEBL, formed in 1992 from three BCCI branches in Pakistan as a susidiary of the state-owned Habib Bank Limited, is the third bank to be privatised by Pakistan after the transfer of the controlling shares of the Muslim Commercial Bank to a private group and of the Allied Bank Ltd to its employees.
